records.source: הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ׀כִּי־ט֭וֹב זַמְּרָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־נָ֝עִים נָאוָ֥ה תְהִלָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Praise Yah, for good [is it] to sing praises [to] our God, for pleasant, fitting [is] praise.
pieces: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! It is good to make music for our God; it is a delight, and praise is fitting.

L.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! For [it is] good to sing praises [to] our God; for [it is] pleasant, praise [is] fitting.

R.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! It is good to sing to our God. It is a delight, and praising {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} is the right thing to do.

decisions.choice: Praise Yah: hallelu-yah, a call to praise the LORD
decisions.reason: The words (hallelu yah) are a command to a group, "praise Yah"; Yah is the short form of the divine name (YHWH). Psalms 146-150 each open and close with this call. Here in Psalm 147 the renderings translate it, as "Praise the LORD", rather than keep it as the borrowed word "Hallelujah".

decisions.choice: for ... for: the reasons for praise, or "how"
decisions.reason: The small word ki usually means "for" or "because", giving the reason for the call to praise; it can also mark an exclamation, "how good!". Either way the line says that praising God is good and fitting.
"Pleasant" (na'im) most likely describes the singing, as in 135:3. It could also describe God, "for he is gracious".
The word (na'wah) is what suits or becomes someone; praise suits God's people (33:1).

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} who counts stars and heals

records.source: בּוֹנֵ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה נִדְחֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל יְכַנֵּֽס׃
records.gloss: Building Jerusalem [is] YHWH; [the] banished of Israel he gathers.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is rebuilding Jerusalem; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is bringing together Israel's scattered exiles.

L.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] building Jerusalem; the banished of Israel {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gathers.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is building up Jerusalem again. He is bringing back the people of Israel who were driven away from their land.

decisions.reason: Isaiah 56:8 calls the LORD the one "who gathers the banished of Israel", in the same words.

decisions.choice: building Jerusalem, gathering exiles: the return from exile
decisions.reason: The words fit the time after the exile in Babylon, when the exiles came home and Jerusalem and its walls were rebuilt (Ezra 1; Nehemiah 2:17; 12:27). The psalm may have been sung then.
The word (nidchim) is people scattered and driven away from their land (Deuteronomy 30:4).
Balanced and Readable bring out that the city is being built again after its ruin (m2).

records.source: הָ֭רֹפֵא לִשְׁב֣וּרֵי לֵ֑ב וּ֝מְחַבֵּ֗שׁ לְעַצְּבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: The one healing [the] broken of heart, and binding up their wounds.
pieces: He heals those whose hearts are crushed and bandages their injuries.

L.3: [He is] the one who heals the broken of heart and binds up their wounds.

R.3: He heals people whose hearts are broken, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts bandages on their wounds.

decisions.choice: the broken of heart: people crushed by grief or shame
decisions.reason: A broken heart is a spirit crushed by sorrow, loss or guilt (34:19; 51:19).
Isaiah 61:1 speaks of one sent "to bind up the broken of heart", with the same words. The God who gathers his scattered people (verse 2) also heals them.
The verb (chavash) is to wrap a wound (Ezekiel 34:16).

records.source: מוֹנֶ֣ה מִ֭סְפָּר לַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים לְ֝כֻלָּ֗ם שֵׁמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃
records.gloss: Counting [the] number of the stars; to all of them names he calls.
pieces: He decides how many stars there are and gives each one its name.

L.4: [He is] counting the number of the stars; to all of them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls names.

R.4: He knows exactly how many stars there are, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has a name for every one of them.

decisions.reason: In Isaiah 40:26 God brings out the stars by number and calls each one by name; no star is missing.

decisions.choice: counting the number: setting or knowing how many
decisions.reason: The words (moneh mispar) can mean that he counts the stars, or that he fixes their number. Either way, what no human can count (Genesis 15:5) he knows.
To give names is to know and to have authority over what is named (Genesis 2:19-20). The God who numbers the stars is the one who heals the broken (verse 3).

records.source: גָּד֣וֹל אֲדוֹנֵ֣ינוּ וְרַב־כֹּ֑חַ לִ֝תְבוּנָת֗וֹ אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
records.gloss: Great [is] our Lord and abundant of strength; to his understanding there [is] no number.
pieces: Our Lord is great and mighty in power; there is no measuring {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding.

L.5: Great [is] our Lord, and abundant in power; to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding [there is] no number.

R.5: Our Lord is great and very powerful. There is no end to what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} understands.

decisions.reason: The word ('adon) is a master or lord; here, as often, it is used of God (8:2).
He knows the number of the stars (verse 4, the same word, mispar), but his own understanding has no number (Isaiah 40:28).

records.source: מְעוֹדֵ֣ד עֲנָוִ֣ים יְהוָ֑ה מַשְׁפִּ֖יל רְשָׁעִ֣ים עֲדֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Relieving [the] humble [is] YHWH, bringing low [the] wicked to [the] ground.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lifts up the lowly and throws the wicked down to the earth.

L.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] relieving [the] humble, bringing [the] wicked down to the ground.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} helps people who are humble, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knocks wicked people down to the ground.

decisions.choice: the humble: the lowly who depend on God
decisions.reason: The word ('anawim) is the poor and powerless who look to God for help (22:27; 37:11).
The verb is the one used in 146:9 for the orphan and the widow.

records.source: עֱנ֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה בְּתוֹדָ֑ה זַמְּר֖וּ לֵאלֹהֵ֣ינוּ בְכִנּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Sing to YHWH with thanksgiving; sing praises to our God with [the] lyre,
pieces: Sing out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with thanks; make music for our God on the lyre,

L.7: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with thanksgiving; make music to our God on the lyre,

R.7: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Play music on the lyre for our God.

decisions.reason: The verb ('anah) usually means "answer"; here it is singing, perhaps singing back and forth (Exodus 15:21; Numbers 21:17). A new call to praise begins the second part of the psalm.
The kinnor was played with the hands or a pick, held while singing (33:2; 1 Samuel 16:23).
Verses 8-9 go on describing "our God", so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: הַֽמְכַסֶּ֬ה שָׁמַ֨יִם׀בְּעָבִ֗ים הַמֵּכִ֣ין לָאָ֣רֶץ מָטָ֑ר הַמַּצְמִ֖יחַ הָרִ֣ים חָצִֽיר׃
records.gloss: the one covering [the] heavens with clouds, the one preparing for the earth rain, the one causing to sprout [on the] mountains grass,
pieces: who wraps the sky in clouds, who gets rain ready for the land, who makes grass sprout on the mountains,

L.8: who covers [the] heavens with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout [on the] mountains,

R.8: He covers the sky with clouds and gets the rain ready for the earth. He makes grass grow on the mountains.

decisions.reason: In a land that depends on rain for its crops, rain was seen as God's gift in its season (Deuteronomy 11:14; 104:13-14).

alternatives: grass, and plants for people's use (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds "and green plants for the service of human beings", words found in 104:14. The renderings follow the Hebrew text.
Readable starts new sentences and says who does this.

records.source: נוֹתֵ֣ן לִבְהֵמָ֣ה לַחְמָ֑הּ לִבְנֵ֥י עֹ֝רֵ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִקְרָֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: giving to [the] animals their food, to [the] young of [the] raven which call.
pieces: who gives the beasts their food and feeds the raven's chicks when they call.

L.9: who gives the animals their food, [and] to the young of the raven that cry out.

R.9: He gives food to the animals. He feeds the baby ravens when they cry for it.

decisions.reason: God asks Job who feeds the raven when its young cry to God (Job 38:41). Jesus points to the ravens that God feeds (Luke 12:24).
The word (behemah) is animals, often cattle and other livestock (104:14).

records.source: לֹ֤א בִגְבוּרַ֣ת הַסּ֣וּס יֶחְפָּ֑ץ לֹֽא־בְשׁוֹקֵ֖י הָאִ֣ישׁ יִרְצֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Not in [the] strength of the horse he delights; not in [the] legs of the man he takes pleasure.
pieces: It is not the power of the horse that delights {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, nor a soldier's strong legs that please {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.10: Not in the strength of the horse does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delight; not in the legs of the man does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} take pleasure.

R.10: He is not impressed by powerful war horses or by soldiers with strong legs.

decisions.choice: the horse and the man: strength for war
decisions.reason: Horses pulled chariots and carried riders in battle, and a soldier on foot needed strong, fast legs (2 Samuel 2:18). Kings trusted in such strength, but God does not (20:8; 33:16-17).

decisions.choice: the man: the warrior on foot
decisions.reason: The word ('ish) is a man; set beside the war horse, it pictures the foot soldier.
Balanced and Readable say what kind of man is meant (m2).

records.source: רוֹצֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־יְרֵאָ֑יו אֶת־הַֽמְיַחֲלִ֥ים לְחַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Taking pleasure [is] YHWH in those fearing him, in those who wait for his loyal love.
pieces: What pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is people who revere {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and look with hope to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love.

L.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} takes pleasure in those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, in those who wait for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is pleased with people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and count on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love.

decisions.choice: taking pleasure: the answer to verse 10
decisions.reason: The same verb (ratsah) as in verse 10: God takes no pleasure in strength for war, but in people who fear him.
The verb (yachal) is to wait with hope (33:18, 22).
The word (chesed) is love that keeps faith, the commitment God has bound himself to toward his people (Exodus 34:6-7). Literal and Balanced say "loyal love".
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: שַׁבְּחִ֣י יְ֭רוּשָׁלִַם אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה הַֽלְלִ֖י אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Extol, Jerusalem, YHWH; praise your God, Zion!
pieces: Jerusalem, glorify {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Zion, praise your God!

L.12: Extol {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion!

R.12: People of Jerusalem, praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! People of Zion, praise your God!

decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation counts verses 1-11 as one psalm and verses 12-20 as another. The Hebrew text has one psalm, and the renderings follow it. A third call to praise begins here.

decisions.choice: extol, praise: commands to the city
decisions.reason: The commands are feminine singular: the city is addressed as a woman, as cities often are in Hebrew poetry (Isaiah 52:1-2).

decisions.choice: People of Jerusalem; People of Zion
decisions.reason: Readable says that the city's people are addressed.

records.source: כִּֽי־חִ֭זַּק בְּרִיחֵ֣י שְׁעָרָ֑יִךְ בֵּרַ֖ךְ בָּנַ֣יִךְ בְּקִרְבֵּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: For he has strengthened [the] bars of your gates; he has blessed your children in your midst.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made the bars of your gates strong and has blessed your children inside your walls.

L.13: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has strengthened the bars of your gates; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has blessed your children within you.

R.13: He has made the bars on the city gates strong. He has blessed the people who live in the city.

decisions.choice: the bars of your gates: the city's defenses
decisions.reason: City gates were shut at night and in war and held by heavy bars (Nehemiah 3; Judges 16:3). Strong bars mean a city safe from attack.

decisions.choice: your children: the people of the city
decisions.reason: The "children" of a city are its people (149:2).

decisions.choice: the city gates; the people who live in the city
alternatives: your gates; your children within you
decisions.reason: Readable speaks about the city rather than to it, to keep the sentences plain.

records.source: הַשָּׂם־גְּבוּלֵ֥ךְ שָׁל֑וֹם חֵ֥לֶב חִ֝טִּ֗ים יַשְׂבִּיעֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: The one making your border peace; [the] fat of wheat he satisfies you [with].
pieces: He keeps your frontiers at peace and satisfies you with the richest wheat.

L.14: [He is] the one who makes your border peace; [with the] fat of wheat {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} satisfies you.

R.14: He keeps the land around the city safe and peaceful. He gives its people plenty of the best wheat to eat.

decisions.choice: the fat of wheat: the best wheat
decisions.reason: "Fat" is the richest part, and so the best (81:17; Deuteronomy 32:14).
The word (gevul) is a border and also the land within it.

decisions.choice: the land around the city; its people
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, Readable speaks about the city rather than to it.

records.source: הַשֹּׁלֵ֣חַ אִמְרָת֣וֹ אָ֑רֶץ עַד־מְ֝הֵרָ֗ה יָר֥וּץ דְּבָרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: The one sending his saying [to the] earth; very quickly runs his word.
pieces: He issues {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} orders to the earth, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word goes out at a run.

L.15: [He is] the one sending {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command [to the] earth; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word runs very swiftly.

R.15: He gives orders to the earth, and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says happens right away.

decisions.reason: The word ('imrah) is something said; here it is God's command to the world, which verses 16-18 show at work in snow, frost, hail and thaw.

decisions.choice: his word runs: what he says is done at once
decisions.reason: The word is pictured as a swift messenger. What God commands happens without delay (33:9; 148:8).

decisions.choice: what he says happens right away
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: הַנֹּתֵ֣ן שֶׁ֣לֶג כַּצָּ֑מֶר כְּ֝פ֗וֹר כָּאֵ֥פֶר יְפַזֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: The one giving snow like wool; frost like ash he scatters.
pieces: He sends snow that lies like wool and strews frost like ash.

L.16: [He is] the one giving snow like wool; frost like ashes {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} scatters.

R.16: He sends snow that looks like wool. He scatters frost like ashes from a fire.

decisions.choice: snow like wool: white and thick
decisions.reason: Wool is a picture of whiteness (Isaiah 1:18) and also of a soft, thick covering.

decisions.choice: frost like ash: a fine powder strewn over the ground
decisions.reason: Frost lies on the ground like ashes scattered from a fire.

records.source: מַשְׁלִ֣יךְ קַֽרְח֣וֹ כְפִתִּ֑ים לִפְנֵ֥י קָ֝רָת֗וֹ מִ֣י יַעֲמֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Throwing his ice like crumbs; before his cold who will stand?
pieces: He flings down {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ice in pieces like crumbs; who can hold out against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cold?

L.17: [He is] throwing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ice like crumbs; before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cold who can stand?

R.17: He throws down hail like little pieces of bread. No one can stand up to the cold {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends.

decisions.reason: The word (qerach) is ice; thrown down in bits, it is hail.
The word (pittim) is morsels of bread (Genesis 18:5 has the singular).

decisions.choice: who will stand: no one can
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one" (76:8; 130:3).

records.source: יִשְׁלַ֣ח דְּבָר֣וֹ וְיַמְסֵ֑ם יַשֵּׁ֥ב ר֝וּח֗וֹ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: He sends his word and melts them; he makes blow his wind; waters flow.
pieces: He sends {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, and the ice thaws; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wind blowing, and the waters run.

L.18: He sends {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word and melts them; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wind blow; [the] waters flow.

R.18: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives an order, and the ice melts. He sends {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wind, and the water flows again.

decisions.choice: them: the snow, frost and ice
decisions.reason: "Them" are the snow, frost and ice of verses 16-17. The word that sent the cold also ends it.

decisions.choice: his wind: the warm wind he sends
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) is wind, breath and spirit; here it is the wind that brings the thaw.
Balanced and Readable say what melts (m1).

records.source: מַגִּ֣יד דְּבָרָ֣יו לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב חֻקָּ֥יו וּ֝מִשְׁפָּטָ֗יו לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Declaring his words to Jacob, his statutes and his judgments to Israel.
pieces: He makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words known to Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings to Israel.

L.19: [He is] declaring {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words to Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments to Israel.

R.19: He has told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words to Jacob's family, the people of Israel. He has given them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decisions.

decisions.choice: his words: the words follow the form to be read
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word in one form and its notes say to read it in another. The renderings follow the form to be read, "his words"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: his words: the same word that rules the weather
decisions.reason: The word (davar) that sends snow and thaw (verses 15, 18) is the word God has spoken to Israel. The God of creation is the God who gave Israel his law.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments: God's laws and rulings
decisions.reason: Two words for God's law (chuqqim, mishpatim), rendered as in Psalm 119: things he has laid down, and his just decisions.

decisions.choice: Jacob's family, the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jacob stands for his descendants.

records.source: לֹ֘א עָ֤שָׂה כֵ֨ן׀לְכָל־גּ֗וֹי וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֥ים בַּל־יְדָע֗וּם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Not he has done thus for any nation, and judgments, they have not known them. Praise Yah!
pieces: No other nation has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} treated this way; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings are unknown to them. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

L.20: Not so has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done for any nation; and [as for] judgments, they have not known them. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

R.20: He has not done this for any other nation. They have never known {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decisions. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

decisions.reason: Moses asks what other nation has a god so near and laws so just (Deuteronomy 4:7-8). Israel's gift is to have been told God's ways.
The Hebrew says "judgments" without "his"; they are the judgments of verse 19.
Balanced and Readable say whose judgments are meant (m2).
